title: Application-layer recon: Header analysis leaks Render state & Cloudflare PoP
summary: HTTP header inspection via curl revealed critical infrastructure behaviors: Cloudflare terminates traffic locally at the Cape Town PoP (CPT), apex radblok.co.za redirects to www with a 301, the web service returns HTTP 503 with 'x-render-routing: suspend-by-user' proving the service was manually suspended in Render, and radblok.onrender.com returns HTTP 404 with 'x-render-routing: no-server' disclosing slug de-allocation.

blocks.label: kali
blocks.text:
$ curl -IL https://radblok.co.za
HTTP/2 301 
date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 19:10:08 GMT
content-type: text/html; charset=utf-8
location: https://www.radblok.co.za/
cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC
server: cloudflare
cf-ray: a43dc3fecfbb039a-CPT
alt-svc: h3=":443"; ma=86400

HTTP/2 503 
date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 19:10:09 GMT
content-type: text/html; charset=utf-8
content-length: 256
x-render-routing: suspend-by-user
cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC
server: cloudflare
cf-ray: a43dc408383bbf11-CPT
alt-svc: h3=":443"; ma=86400

blocks.label: kali
blocks.text:
$ curl -IL https://radblok.onrender.com
HTTP/2 404 
date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 19:10:37 GMT
content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
content-length: 10
x-content-type-options: nosniff
x-render-routing: no-server
cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC
server: cloudflare
cf-ray: a43dc4b83a3abf11-CPT
alt-svc: h3=":443"; ma=86400

head: Header / Signal
Value
Recon & Security Meaning
rows: **Cape Town Point of Presence (PoP)**. Even though Render's origin VMs reside in GCP US West 1 (Oregon), Cloudflare terminates TLS locally in South Africa (CPT airport code) to optimize edge latency.
**Application State Disclosure**. Render custom header confirms the target service exists on Render but has been manually suspended/paused by the account owner.
**Subdomain Mismatch / Slug De-allocation**. `radblok.onrender.com` does not have an active service bound to that exact slug; the service may use a generated hash slug or only bind the custom domain.
**Apex-to-WWW Canonicalization**. The apex domain redirects to `www` via HTTP 301.
**HTTP/3 (QUIC) Supported**. Cloudflare advertises HTTP/3 availability over UDP port 443.

blocks.text: Examining the HTTP/2 503 response reveals an absence of standard defensive HTTP security headers:

head: Header
Status
Risk / Function
rows: Browsers are not instructed to enforce HTTPS-only connections for future visits.
No policy defining trusted sources for scripts, frames, or styles.
No explicit protection against clickjacking/framing (unless defined by HTML meta tags).
Lacks protection against MIME-sniffing attacks on the main error page.

blocks.text: When an application is suspended or served via proxy error pages, CDN/PaaS default error responders often omit custom application security headers configured inside the backend app code.

items: Layer 7 recon successfully extracted operational state without invasive scanning.
`x-render-routing: suspend-by-user` confirms the backend project status on Render.
Cloudflare's edge PoP (`CPT` / Cape Town) confirmed geographic edge routing.
Next step: Inspect TLS certificate details and Subject Alternative Names (SANs) to see what other hostnames are bound to the certificate.
